feature.summary: In a Slack channel, when a person mentions AGI again inside a thread where AGI already ran a task for them, the new message continues the same AGI conversation. Answer-mode and direct-message runs keep no session; they rebuild context from Slack history. Web only; desktop shows the same hosted app.

purpose.what_it_does: Maps a Slack thread to one AGI conversation for task-mode runs, so follow-ups add to the same conversation (apps/web/lib/slack/slack-tasks.ts:93-119,167-174). For answers, it re-reads the Slack thread or recent history on each message (apps/web/lib/slack/slack-context.ts:92-122).
purpose.why_it_exists: S106.23 requires each channel thread to map to one persistent agent session so follow-ups continue it. Without it each mention would start a fresh conversation with no memory of the task.
purpose.who_uses_it: A linked Slack user working with AGI in a channel thread.
problems_solved: Losing earlier work when asking a follow-up
Many one-off conversations for one thread
use_cases: Ask AGI to draft a report, then reply in the thread 'make it shorter' with a mention
Ask a question in a thread and follow up; AGI reads the thread to see earlier messages
Open the single AGI conversation to see the whole thread's work

where_to_find_it: Slack: reply in the thread of an earlier AGI task and mention the app. A plain reply without a mention is not read: only app_mention and direct-message events are taken up (apps/web/lib/slack/slack-events.ts:67-68).
Web: the one conversation appears in the normal conversation list; Desktop shows the same hosted web app (doc: AGENTS.md section 5).
prerequisites: Channel mode is task (or default) and task is available for the account (slack-assistant.ts:354-362)
The first message in the thread ran in task mode and created an agent run (slack-tasks.ts:169-192)
Same AGI person, workspace, installation and channel (slack-tasks.ts:105-117)
screens_and_controls: No dedicated control. The thread itself is the control.
journey: Person mentions AGI in a channel; task mode starts and a conversation is created titled from the first line (slack-tasks.ts:39-43,171-174).
Person mentions AGI again in that thread.
AGI looks for the earliest earlier run in the same thread by the same person and reuses its conversation (slack-tasks.ts:93-119).
The new request is saved as a user message and a new agent run is created in that conversation (slack-tasks.ts:175-189).
feedback_and_outputs: The answer in the thread with a link to the task (slack-assistant.ts:151-155)
The AGI conversation grows with each follow-up (slack-tasks.ts:175-179,216-222)
settings: Per-channel mode (F106-07): answer mode disables sessions
No setting for context sizes; they are constants (apps/web/lib/slack/slack-config.ts:32-41)

working: Task runs find an earlier run in the same thread and reuse its conversation; otherwise create one (slack-tasks.ts:167-174).

Lookup matches thread root as earlier.thread_ts or earlier.message_ts, excludes the current run, and requires same user, organization, installation, channel and a non-deleted conversation (slack-tasks.ts:98-117).
Answer-mode and DM runs read Slack: thread up to 40 messages (20 in DMs), DM history up to 20 messages within 12 hours, channel history last 10 (slack-context.ts:92-122; slack-config.ts:32-41).
incomplete: Only task-mode runs get a persistent AGI conversation; answer-mode runs have none (slack-assistant.ts:401; slack-tasks.ts).
Continuity is per person: another person mentioning AGI in the same thread gets their own conversation, because the lookup requires the same user_id (slack-tasks.ts:109).
A follow-up needs a mention; thread replies without a mention are ignored (slack-events.ts:67-68).
Direct messages never use task mode (slackRunModeFor with no policy and task unavailable for DMs, slack-assistant.ts:354-362), so DM threads are answer-only [inferred].
disconnected_or_disabled: Brief says missing; the code exists for task mode, so the brief is out of date [inferred].
not_available: Teams and email thread continuity: no code (F106-09, F106-10)
Mobile, CLI, VS Code, Chrome: n/a per brief

established.statement: Each channel conversation or thread maps to one persistent agent session, so follow-ups in the thread continue it.
Only task-mode runs are linked to a conversation; the lookup reuses an earlier run's conversation in the same thread.
Answer-mode runs rebuild context from Slack history each message.

acceptance_criteria: Two mentions in one thread by one person in task mode produce one conversation with both requests.
A mention in a new thread or a top-level message creates a new conversation.
Another Slack workspace or channel never reuses the conversation.
A deleted conversation is not reused; a new one is created.
In answer mode no conversation is created and the second answer sees earlier thread messages.
Two people in one thread each get their own conversation.
inferred: The thread should survive the first run failing: a run with no agent_run_id is skipped by the join [inferred from the join on cloud_agent_runs].
proposed: [proposed] Share one conversation per thread across people in the same workspace, if the product wants that.
[proposed] Also read unmentioned thread replies once AGI has joined a thread.

steps.what_happens: Slack posts an app_mention event with thread_ts; server verifies and queues handling after the response.
AGI resolves the link, mode and creates a run row with channel, message and thread timestamps.
Context is read from Slack's API (thread or history).
When the model route is chosen, the observer looks up an earlier conversation, else inserts one, saves the user message and creates an agent run.
The answer is saved as an assistant message and the agent run moves to ready_for_review.

execution_and_data_flow.models_and_providers: The model is picked per turn by server routing and stored on the conversation when it is created (slack-tasks.ts:171-174). A follow-up reuses the conversation but picks its model again [inferred from selectRoute running each turn]. No Local or own-key route found.

corrections.what_the_code_shows: Web code fully implements thread reuse for task mode (findSlackThreadConversation, routed observer) and has a test file; section 3 itself says so.
corrections.correction: Web: partial (task-mode channel runs only; answer-mode and DM runs keep no conversation). Desktop is not separately built, it shows the hosted app. Status table and 'not built on any app' should be updated.

missing_facts: Free and other non-Pro plans are refused for every Slack run (slack_app uses PRO_TIERS), so no thread continuity or even answers exist for them: packages/contracts/types/src/billing-catalog.ts:341,360; apps/web/lib/slack/slack-assistant-turn.ts:415-421.

The conversation is created in the run's organization with model from the first routed turn, and an agent run is created only when the model route is chosen (observer.routed); a run refused before routing (plan, compute access) leaves no agent_run_id, so later follow-ups cannot join to it: apps/web/lib/slack/slack-tasks.ts:167-190; slack-assistant-turn.ts:415-437.
Task runs also read Slack context (buildSlackTurnContext runs before slackTask), so Slack API reads occur for task runs too, not only answer/DM runs: apps/web/lib/slack/slack-assistant.ts:~385-400.
